sections.html:
The Lee County Clerk of Court records deeds, mortgages and similar instruments through its Official Records Services office. Two counters take paper: 2115 Second Street in Fort Myers, and the Lee County Government Center at 1039 SE 9th Place in Cape Coral.

Mailed documents go to Lee County Clerk of Courts, PO Box 2278, Fort Myers, FL 33902. Electronic recording is also open, described as a secure online route that skips mail, couriers and office visits. Staff at the clerk's office will not fill out forms for you and suggest hiring a professional who prepares deeds regularly. For a sale that is sound advice: a wrong legal description or a missing witness line gets the deed returned and can push back the closing. Every instrument needs an accurate legal description, and each name must be spelled the way it appears in the signature block.

  • In person at either counter.
  • By mail, with a self-addressed stamped envelope.
  • Drop box, with the documents, payment and return envelope sealed together.
  • Electronic filing through the clerk's E-Record service.

sections.h2: What a Lee County deed must contain
sections.html:
A deed has to meet section 695.26 of the Florida Statutes, and the clerk's checklist spells out the details. A rejected deed costs days, so go down the list before anyone signs.

  • A line naming whoever prepared the deed, with that person's address.
  • Printed names and mailing addresses for the sellers (grantors) and buyers (grantees).
  • Seller signatures with printed names beneath.
  • Two witnesses, each with a printed name and address under the signature.
  • A full notary acknowledgment: names, date, notary signature, printed name, commission expiration and seal.
  • Empty space at the top right corner of the first page, 3 by 3 inches, and 1 by 3 inches on later pages.

Each signature on a transfer needs two witnesses, although a corporation signs under its seal instead. State the sale price or consideration on the deed or in a cover letter, because the clerk needs it to work out the tax. The Florida statute on land conveyances likewise calls for two subscribing witnesses.

On letter or legal paper, the clerk charges $10.00 for the first page and $8.50 for each page after. Each name beyond four adds $1.00 for indexing.

sections.h2: Taxes due when a deed or mortgage is recorded
sections.html:
Documentary stamps are collected when the deed is recorded: 70 cents for each $100, or part of $100, on warranty deeds, quit claim deeds and comparable transfers. The clerk forwards the money to the Department of Revenue.

Mortgages work differently. Intangible tax on a note secured by a mortgage is paid at recording at 2 mills, or $.002 per dollar financed. The Department of Revenue adds that documentary stamps on a mortgage and note run 35 cents per $100 secured, with a $2,450 cap on a note and no cap on a mortgage.

Everyone named on a document is liable for its tax, whichever party agrees to pay. Many Lee County purchase contracts put the deed stamps on the seller, but the contract is what settles it. State guidance treats an estate representative's deed under a probated will as not taxable and exempts a divorce deed for the marital home.

sections.h2: Recording a death certificate or other documents
sections.html:
It can be done, with conditions. An uncertified copy of a death certificate cannot be recorded unless a court or the Attorney General orders otherwise. A Florida certificate offered for recording has to be a certified copy approved by the Department of Health that omits confidential cause-of-death details. One that includes the cause of death will be refused.

Out-of-state death certificates must be certified copies from that state's agencies or courts. Heirs selling a parent's Lee County house usually need this paper, so request a recordable version at the start. Order several copies, since the county keeps the one it records and a title company may want its own. Ask the Florida Department of Health, not the clerk, how to get the version without the cause of death.

Some rules cover every recording. Names must read the same in the body of the document and under each signature. Any instrument moving an interest in real property, mortgages aside, must show the grantee's mailing address. Wills, plats, court orders and instruments signed outside Florida are treated as exceptions to some formatting rules. Documents mailed without a stamped return envelope are held, and anything still held after 90 days is destroyed.

Filing a foreclosure or other real property case costs $470.00 when the claim is below $50,000, $975.00 from $50,000 to $250,000 and $1,975.00 above $250,000. The clerk charges $70.00 to hold the judicial sale and asks for a $600.00 deposit toward the notice of sale.

A recorded lis pendens tells buyers that a lawsuit touches the parcel. By statute the sale comes 20 to 35 days after judgment, and an electronic auction is allowed. An owner behind on a mortgage can try for a pre-sale deal that pays off the loan from the sale proceeds.

Eviction filings in county court cost $185.00, and the sheriff's fee for a writ of possession is $90.00, subject to change by the sheriff. A landlord selling a rented Lee County house should expect the buyer to request lease copies, so pull them before listing. Buyers also ask whether any tenant has been served a notice, and the answer should match the court docket.

sections.h2: Steps before you sign a Lee County deed
sections.html:
A short routine keeps a sale from stalling at the recording counter.

  1. Get the legal description from your current deed and copy it exactly.
  2. Confirm every seller and buyer name, spelled as it will appear in the signature blocks.
  3. Line up two witnesses and a notary for the signing.
  4. Decide who pays the stamp tax and write that into the contract.
  5. Ask the title company whether it will record electronically or whether you must deliver the original.
  6. Keep a copy of the recorded deed once it posts.

A cash sale skips lender underwriting, so the deed and the recording paperwork often become the slowest remaining pieces. Having them right the first time saves that time.

faqs.q: Who records deeds in Lee County, Florida?
faqs.a: The Lee County Clerk of Court, through Official Records Services. Filing is available in Fort Myers, in Cape Coral, by mail, by drop box or electronically.

faqs.q: How many witnesses does a Lee County deed need?
faqs.a: Two. The checklist also asks for a full notary acknowledgment, a prepared-by line, and mailing addresses for sellers and buyers.

faqs.q: What is the Lee County recording fee?
faqs.a: Standard recording runs $10.00 for page one and $8.50 for each page after, with $1.00 for each name over four. Deed documentary stamps are billed separately at $0.70 per $100.00.

faqs.q: Can I record an uncertified death certificate in Lee County?
faqs.a: No, unless a court or the Attorney General orders it. The certificate must be certified, and a Florida one must leave out confidential cause-of-death information.

faqs.q: Will the Lee County clerk mail back my recorded document?
faqs.a: Only if you enclose a self-addressed stamped envelope. Otherwise the clerk holds it, and anything held longer than 90 days is destroyed.
